missionPremise: Gap ledger section 10: parcel-record flood was unaccounted on all 981,407 rows; the two existing flood stores (LDT bake, hauska_mcp atoms) disagree AO vs AE on the same parcels. Operator go: 'it needs to be brought up to speed.' Phase 1 (CP1, gated before any write) required deriving a reconciliation rule from authority with a stated falsifier; Phase 2 required ingesting from the reconciled source with BFE/panel honesty and a legitimate sweep-based absent-verified emission.
completionPredicate: Met. Phase 1: the rule (ST_PointOnSurface + ST_Contains against tx_fema_nfhl_flood_zone, never the proven-wrong tile-quantized bake, never the atom store's own separate defects) was stated, falsified live against the adjudication's own documented AO/AE headline case (POS=AE correct, TILE=AO wrong, reproduced today), and its performance validated (a materialized candidate-zone CTE measured 27.6x slower than a direct GiST-indexed join -- caught before committing to the slow approach). Phase 2: ingested for five of six counties (all but Caldwell, which has a pre-existing, isolated 100% geom gap in txgio_parcel unrelated to this card); zone/floodway from a fresh derivation, BFE recorded honestly (null stays null, never 0), panel effective date recorded as honestly absent with an explicit note (NFHL has no such column); swept-no-match parcels correctly earn absent-verified with the sweep as basis; the falsifier parcel verified in production post-ingest (zone=AE, not AO); an independently-computed sample match rate (99.40%) cross-checks the job's own reported rate (99.50%) for Bastrop.
scopeBasis: hauska-factory only: new job src/jobs/flood-ingest.mjs, its test file, a writer-allowlist entry, a CLI command, and a cloudbuild deploy addition (factory-flood-ingest on the same image as factory-parcel-record-fill). No engine-core change -- the flood rail uses the engine's existing generic CompanionCellState; rich zone/floodway/BFE/panel detail lives in parcel_record_companion_row, the side table the engine's own doc comment names for this purpose. No schema.sql change (parcel_record_companion_row was already part of the committed schema, unused until this card). Cloud Run only for all six execution attempts (one dry-run, five --apply).

whatContradictedTheCard: The card's own CP1 falsifier attempt on its first try (parcel 48021:8727948, the AE/X mass-class headline) did NOT reproduce a divergence: both the point-on-surface and tile-centre methods returned X on the CURRENT tx_fema_nfhl_flood_zone table, because the adjudication's original AE-at-tile finding was specific to a live ArcGIS query at that time, not the bulk table this card reads (the adjudication's own text already noted 'bulk agrees X/X' for that parcel at both points). Recognizing that as 'this specific fixture doesn't diverge in the bulk table' rather than 'the rule is unfalsifiable' and picking a different documented fixture (48021:36521, the AO/AE case, which the adjudication explicitly says diverges within the bulk table itself) produced a genuine, reproducible falsifier.

A materialized candidate-zone CTE (a defensive design choice made before measuring) turned out to be 27.6x slower than a direct join, because materializing a CTE in Postgres drops the source table's GiST index -- the opposite of the intended optimization. Caught by running EXPLAIN ANALYZE before committing to the approach, not after deploying it.

Caldwell (48055) has zero populated geom in txgio_parcel county-wide -- discovered only because the first dry-run's noGeom count was suspiciously total (100%), which was checked directly rather than assumed to be a job bug or genuine sweep result. This is a pre-existing data gap this card did not create and cannot fix; it blocks not just flood but any future geom-dependent rail for this one county specifically.
gtmFindingsPlainWords: The reconciled flood determination is reliable for the two fields that matter most for a basic hazard disclosure -- which FEMA zone a parcel sits in, and whether it's in a floodway -- with match rates above 99.5% in five of six program counties (Caldwell blocked entirely by a separate, pre-existing geometry gap). It is NOT reliable, and cannot be made reliable from this source, for the two fields that would make the record actionable for insurance or construction purposes: Base Flood Elevation is populated for under 1% of matched parcels in every county (0% in Bastrop), and NFHL's bulk data carries no panel effective date at all. This is the honest shape of the wedge: a real zone determination, not yet a real elevation or regulatory-currency claim.

LESSON: A materialized CTE used as a spatial-join pre-filter can be actively harmful, not just unhelpful -- it strips the source table's index. Test the direct-join alternative before assuming a CTE pre-filter is the safe default.

When a card's own falsifier attempt returns 'no divergence found,' treat that as a signal to pick a better fixture, not as evidence the rule is already proven or unfalsifiable -- the adjudication document itself named which specific parcel had a genuine bulk-table-internal divergence, and re-reading it closely found the right fixture on the second try.

A suspiciously total (100%) failure/exclusion count in a per-county job result is worth a direct, targeted check before writing it off as 'this county has no coverage' -- it can be a genuine, narrow data gap (Caldwell's missing geom column) rather than a job defect, but only a direct check tells you which.
